reading: on the residualised target the four contributions are +0.007 / +0.012 / +0.004 / +0.027, total +0.050. The filter is the largest single step (+0.027), the inversion next (+0.012), and both are highly significant in the fold-paired sense -- but note that the total advantage over their kernel (+0.042 vs their CBIG re-run 0.6798) is 'significant' only for the filtered arm; the unfiltered chain's +0.015 was not (NB t 1.33, parallel measurement).
data_handling: covariate CSV is HCP restricted-shaped: used on the pod only and deleted after the run; the repo holds per-fold scores, no subject-level covariates
_correction: the stored NB_t column was the PER-SEED NAIVE t (mean(d)/sqrt(var(d)/m) with m counted per seed), not the Nadeau-Bengio corrected value. Per-fold naive t would be 21.0 for the filter step; the exact corrected form mean(d)/sqrt((1/m + n_te/n_tr)*var(d)) with m=600 fold differences and n_te/n_tr=0.1111 gives 2.55. The shrink factor between per-fold naive and corrected is 8.23; between my stored per-seed value and corrected it is 17.9.
note_on_significance: after correction: the filter step +0.0267 is NB t 2.55 (borderline, p~0.011); the inversion +0.0118 is NB t 0.91 (not significant); the 5% mix and the kernel-construction step are NB t ~2.1 and ~1.8. So of the four steps, only the filter is individually significant at the conventional level, and even it is borderline once the family of four steps is considered.

column_names.naive_t: per-seed naive t (as originally stored, inflated)

_note: the parallel session recomputed from the same per-fold data and got the identical 2.55 / p 0.011 for the filter step, so the corrected column is confirmed by two implementations.
